title: Turnip, fennel and barley pot with white beans

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple such as vegetable stock, tinned cannellini beans and pearl barley.

supermarket.reason: Turnips, fennel, kale, barley and tinned beans are all everyday supermarket items at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large lidded pan, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple softening and simmering.

works.reason: The amounts suit four for lunch: 150g barley, 500g turnips and a tin of beans in 1.2l stock, simmered covered for 35 minutes, gives tender barley in a brothy pot.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers the chopping, the peeling and cubing of 500g turnips and the 10-minute softening, and the 40 minutes of cooking matches the 35 plus 5 minutes in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears apart from water, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming barley and turnip pot suits mid-October, and the turnips are the main vegetable rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Barley, beans, turnips and kale make a filling, balanced vegan lunch a family would happily eat again.
